prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider fails to transparently refresh tokens after the process restarts and state is reloaded from TokenStorage: _initialize() never recomputes token_expiry_time from the stored token's expires_in, so is_token_valid() treats an expired token as valid and the proactive-refresh branch in async_auth_flow never fires; separately, authorization-server metadata is also not restored, forcing rediscovery. Net effect: every restart triggers a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (4 PRs)

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe
prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: All three fix the same bug: MCPError (and its subclass UrlElicitationRequiredError) raises TypeError on unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ tries to reconstruct via cls(*self.args), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures (e.g. UrlElicitationRequiredError takes (elicitations, message) not (code, message, data)). #2555 explicitly refs #2431 for this; #3262 has the identical PR title targeting the same class; #2478 adds the same kind of generic reconstruction dispatch (_restore_mcp_error) at the MCPError base level, which would also resolve #2431 as a side effect. (3 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3262's __reduce__ is defined once on the base MCPError class and reconstructs via MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(*args) + dict restore, so it works uniformly for any subclass without calling the subclass constructor at all — its test file imports NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError to prove this. #2555 only overrides __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so it leaves every other MCPError subclass (e.g. NoBackChannelError) still broken on pickle. #2478 also fixes at the base-class level but its _restore_mcp_error helper dispatches by exact type and calls each subclass's from_error_data/from_error classmethod, which requires every current and future subclass to expose a compatible reconstruction classmethod — a narrower contract than 3262's constructor-independent approach.

members.cluster_pick_reason: 3262's __reduce__ is defined once on the base MCPError class and reconstructs via MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(*args) + dict restore, so it works uniformly for any subclass without calling the subclass constructor at all — its test file imports NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError to prove this. #2555 only overrides __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so it leaves every other MCPError subclass (e.g. NoBackChannelError) still broken on pickle. #2478 also fixes at the base-class level but its _restore_mcp_error helper dispatches by exact type and calls each subclass's from_error_data/from_error classmethod, which requires every current and future subclass to expose a compatible reconstruction classmethod — a narrower contract than 3262's constructor-independent approach.

members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both PRs rewrite the same block of RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py that decides what happens when a request is cancelled. clusters.pick_reason: 3243 replaces context.lock's anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) and adds a separate flow_lock scoped only to refresh/authorization transitions; this removes the task-ownership constraint of anyio.Lock, which matters because httpx can resume or close the auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock. 2858 and 3252 both keep the original anyio.Lock and only reposition where it is acquired/released within async_auth_flow (2858 narrows the `async with` block's scope; 3252 moves the `yield request` and response handling outside the lock entirely), so neither addresses the underlying task-locality assumption that anyio.Lock carries.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 detects the duplicate by reusing the existing `str(message.id)` key, which was already collapsing distinct JSON-RPC ids (int `1` and string "1" hash to the same key) — so its guard would falsely 400 a legitimate request whose id merely stringifies the same as an in-flight one, and it leaves the id "_GET_stream" free to collide with the reserved standalone-GET stream slot. #3221 replaces the key scheme with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key` ("i:" / "s:" prefix) that keeps int and str ids distinct and is proven never to equal `GET_STREAM_KEY`, so it closes the same race without introducing those two false-positive/collision cases.

members.cluster_pick_reason: 3262's __reduce__ is defined once on the base MCPError class and reconstructs via MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(*args) + dict restore, so it works uniformly for any subclass without calling the subclass constructor at all — its test file imports NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError to prove this. #2555 only overrides __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so it leaves every other MCPError subclass (e.g. NoBackChannelError) still broken on pickle. #2478 also fixes at the base-class level but its _restore_mcp_error helper dispatches by exact type and calls each subclass's from_error_data/from_error classmethod, which requires every current and future subclass to expose a compatible reconstruction classmethod — a narrower contract than 3262's constructor-independent approach.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both PRs rewrite the same block of RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py that decides what happens when a request is cancelled. Today that method sends an error response to indicate cancellation, which the server.py duplicate-suppression comment touched by #2493 shows is spec-non-compliant (receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request). #2493 fixes this by deleting the error-response code entirely (send nothing). #2514 touches the identical code region (same guard clause at the top of cancel(), same method body where the response used to be sent) but instead replaces it with construction and sending of a proper notifications/cancelled message via the newly-imported CancelledNotificationParams, and extends the fix to cover request-timeout cancellation in addition to caller/peer-initiated cancellation.

clusters.pick_reason: 3243 replaces context.lock's anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) and adds a separate flow_lock scoped only to refresh/authorization transitions; this removes the task-ownership constraint of anyio.Lock, which matters because httpx can resume or close the auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock. 2858 and 3252 both keep the original anyio.Lock and only reposition where it is acquired/released within async_auth_flow (2858 narrows the `async with` block's scope; 3252 moves the `yield request` and response handling outside the lock entirely), so neither addresses the underlying task-locality assumption that anyio.Lock carries.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 detects the duplicate by reusing the existing `str(message.id)` key, which was already collapsing distinct JSON-RPC ids (int `1` and string "1" hash to the same key) — so its guard would falsely 400 a legitimate request whose id merely stringifies the same as an in-flight one, and it leaves the id "_GET_stream" free to collide with the reserved standalone-GET stream slot. #3221 replaces the key scheme with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key` ("i:" / "s:" prefix) that keeps int and str ids distinct and is proven never to equal `GET_STREAM_KEY`, so it closes the same race without introducing those two false-positive/collision cases.
